overview.text: The Yaroslavl Great Panagia is a monumental medieval icon now in the Tretyakov Gallery. Its museum title is Mother of God of the Incarnation, with Great Panagia in parentheses. It is distinct from the Yaroslavl Tenderness icon.
overview.reason: Necessary concise account of the named copyrighted publication; full-text reproduction permission has not been established. Traditional events and published interpretations remain attributed.

blocks.text: Mary stands frontally with hands raised in prayer. Christ appears in a medallion before her and blesses with both hands; angels occupy the upper corners. The museum discusses the familiar term Orans while noting that scholarly names for this particular composition have varied.

blocks.text: The gallery dates the panel to the first quarter of the thirteenth century, perhaps around 1224. It was rediscovered at Yaroslavl’s Transfiguration monastery in 1919 and entered the gallery in 1930. The proposed connection with the monastery cathedral remains a probable attribution, not an established commission record.

blocks.text: The museum’s explanation centers on the Incarnation and its liturgical significance. It interprets Mary’s prayerful pose in relation to the intercession of the Church and discusses the Child’s episcopal gesture. These are attributed museum interpretations of this object; no unsupported color code or additional symbolism is supplied.
